instruction: Poubis Provisions, Inc. is the target of a pending acquisition, and we need a clear view of where it stands under its master services agreement with Gibeis Cold Logistics, LLC, where Poubis is the customer. Please review the full matter folder: poubis_gibeis_master_services_agreement.md, gibeis_holdings_parent_guaranty.md, gibeis_poubis_side_letter_oct2026.md, and partnership_press_release_mar2024.md. Then prepare a memo to me that sets out each issue you identify. For each one, give the document and section where it appears, explain why it matters to Poubis, particularly with the acquisition pending, and recommend a fix. Keep each entry short enough that I can lift it straight into advice to the client. Where something is unclear on the face of the documents, or depends on facts we don't have, say so, and list what we would need to ask the client to confirm. Please flag anything you think needs attention before signing or closing at the top of the memo.

rubric.text: The response concludes that Ostrander's acquisition of Poubis is a change of control that the MSA deems an assignment requiring Gibeis's prior written consent, and that no such consent has been obtained. It identifies MSA Section 15.2 as the location, explains why this matters to Poubis with the closing pending, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the MSA exclusivity, read with the 'Affiliate' definition covering future controlling entities, extends to Poubis's future parents across North America (including Ostrander after closing), beyond the Mid-Atlantic scope described in the press release. It identifies MSA Section 3.1 (with Section 1.1) as the location, explains why this matters to Poubis, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the MSA automatically renews for successive three-year terms unless non-renewal notice is given in the 120-to-90-day window, which for the term ending February 28, 2027 runs from about October 31 to November 30, 2026. It identifies MSA Section 2.2 as the location, explains why this matters to Poubis, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the side letter narrows the Cargo Loss exclusion from the liability cap to losses caused by Gibeis's gross negligence or willful misconduct, so spoilage from ordinary negligent temperature excursions is subject to the 12-month fee cap. It identifies Side Letter Section 2 as the location, explains why this matters to Poubis, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the Parent Guaranty covers only 'Covered Goods' (goods at or below -18°C), so Gibeis Holdings Corp. does not guarantee obligations relating to chilled goods that fall within the MSA's 'Cargo' definition. It identifies Parent Guaranty Section 1 (with Section 8) as the location, explains why this matters to Poubis, and recommends a fix.
The response states that Ostrander Foods Group, Inc. is the pending acquirer of Poubis.
The response states that the MSA defines 'Cargo' to include both chilled and frozen goods tendered to Gibeis.
The response is a memo addressed to the supervising partner, and its opening section flags the items that need attention before signing or closing.
The response includes a list of questions or facts to confirm with the client.
The response claims that the October 2026 side letter grants Gibeis's consent to the Ostrander change of control.
The response claims that, after the side letter, Cargo Loss caused by Gibeis's ordinary negligence remains excluded from the liability cap.
